Michael Dublin

GRE candidate for US Senate, North Carolina · Open seat

Retired public school teacher

Michael Dublin is the Green Party nominee for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. He is a retired North Carolina public school teacher who taught for nearly 25 years, has led a volunteer prison ministry for more than two decades, and co-chairs the Black Caucus of the North Carolina Green Party. He is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot with Roy Cooper (DEM), Michael Whatley (REP), and Shannon W. Bray (LIB) for the seat held by Thom Tillis, who is not running again.

Where Dublin stands

Hurricane Helene recovery / FEMA
Says two years is too long to wait for recovery. Proposes cutting red tape to send aid straight to families, holding hearings in the mountains, and publishing what each agency promised next to what it delivered.
Cost of living / inflation
Proposes capping prescription drug prices, banning price gouging on groceries and rent, breaking up food and housing monopolies, and raising the federal minimum wage.
Military spending / health care
Proposes cutting the military budget and moving that money to universal health care and public housing.
Immigration enforcement
Opposes current federal enforcement actions and calls for real due process, no raids on churches or schools, no separating children from parents, consequences for officers who break the law, and an end to private detention contracts.
Campaign finance
Refuses all corporate PAC and lobbyist money, and calls himself "the best candidate money can't buy."
Energy, climate and data centers
Supports a Green New Deal and proposes banning AI data centers, which he says drain North Carolina's water and energy.
Elections and voting
Supports proportional representation and ranked-choice voting.
Reparations / economic justice
Supports lineage-based reparations as part of a broader economic justice platform.
Foreign policy
Proposes ending U.S. funding for what he calls genocide abroad and moving those resources to housing, health care, and education.
